english.title: Cause unauthorised use of premises - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) caused premises, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PREMISES..), to be used to

(A)_[operate a casino]_
(B)_[provide facilities for the playing of bingo]_
(C)_[make a gaming machine available for use]_
(D)_[provide facilities for gaming, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_
(E)_[provide facilities for betting, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_

which were not excepted by provisions contained in the Gambling Act 2005
english.legislation: Contrary to section 37(1) and (8) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
caused unlicenced premises to be used to
operate a casino OR
provide facilities for the playing of bingo OR
make a gaming machine available for use OR
provide other facilities for gaming OR
provide facilities for betting

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Section 37(1)(e) of the Gambling Act 2005 states that providing facilities for betting will include making or accepting bets, acting as a betting intermediary or the provision of other facilities for the making or accepting of bets.
(ii) Section 37(7) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides other premises which are exempted from this offence.
(iii) A licensing authority may institute criminal proceedings in respect of this offence, section 346(1) of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five on the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
